title: TW Hangouts   |   Is TDD dead? [Part III]
summary: Beck, Fowler and DHH discuss testing trade-offs: feedback frequency, fidelity, overhead and lifespan, and whether programmer testing made teams drop QA.

assertions.quote: there's a Continuum of lifespan and and lifespan isn't just measured in years

verdicts.note: A decision framework rather than a measurable claim.

assertions.quote: to be able to run the tests and go okay I don't have to worry about stuff breaking elsewhere is such a magnificent plus
looking at the page seeing how it feels clicking around it's not something that's conducive to tests

verdicts.note: Tests check specified behaviour; user value and design health need other feedback, though some tests target design.

assertions.quote: it gave them overconfidence I think it gave them overconfidence in the quality with which they can produce software through testing

verdicts.note: Anecdotal; some companies did cut QA, but no study links this to measured quality loss.

assertions.quote: you can't on the one hand claim well we need 100% coverage because that's our design methodology

verdicts.note: A logical argument about methodology consistency rather than a measurable outcome.

assertions.quote: programmers accepting responsibility for the quality of their work that that was a huge step forward

verdicts.note: Widely agreed from experience; little direct measurement comparing the two arrangements.

In a short lean-techniques trial on two two-person teams, moving responsibility for measuring quality from the manager to the workers gave a quicker and more thorough response to defects, but one team kept making errors and the study was terminated early.

assertions.quote: we can get some answers in you know hours

verdicts.note: Test automation shortens feedback cycles in DORA and industrial reports; the gain depends on suite quality.

assertions.quote: the on call um uh is the feedback loop that teaches you uh what tests you didn't write

verdicts.note: A reasonable mechanism consistent with DevOps practice; not measured.

assertions.quote: all your tests are [ __ ] green but they're not finding all the problems
